data.name: Torn Familjen
data.detailed_description:
Torn Familjen tells the story of Cathrin, a student of magic whose abundant generosity ends up getting her in big trouble...

She must set off on a journey that ends up taking her to all sorts of places, in order to find some way to atone for her mistake. Along the way, she will make new friends, and new enemies, too. Fortunately, there's no shortage of fighting skill amongst the group she ends up assembling.

((Please note that while flashing lights have been kept to a minimum, some mild screen flashes were simply impossible to remove. Players with photosensitive epilepsy or similar conditions should exercise caution, and are recommended to keep the game screen at its default small size, just to be safe.))

Features:
  • Easy-to-learn Difficult-to-master turn-based strategy combat system.
  • Five difficulties, ranging from a newcomer-friendly Easy, to Hard for RPG fans, to Insane for ravenous strategic challenge seekers!
  • Minimal necessary grinding.
  • Tough optional bosses.
  • Choose how to play, using attack- or defence-oriented equipment for each character, and attach Runes that grant specific benefits!
  • Charming characters and engaging story.
  • Inspired by masterpieces such as Xenoblade Chronicles, and Tales.

data.short_description: A stylised JRPG-style game, in which you guide Cathrin, a budding mage, through a range of environments, taking on big bosses and uncovering the secrets of the magical world of Taika.

reviews.review:
well, it's definitely an rpg maker game alright

pros:
pretty okay battle system. i played through a part of the game on hard difficulty, and it sure tests your strategy all right. while difficult, i wouldn't say it's unfair
cons:
confusing mechanics. no idea what status effects like wind icon, rock icon, and monster icon do. i may of missed a list of status ailments/effects, but not even the readme that came with the game said anything about debuffs
pricing. i feel rpg maker games shouldn't be priced to begin with unless most of their assets are made from the ground up. a game like lisa barely passes that line with pretty obvious yanfly plugins though is still a fun experience with good writing, artstyle, gameplay etc. a game like omori meanwhile is well worth its price owing to how much was put into that game

overall, if this game was free, i'd recommend it if you were moderately interested. otherwise, i wouldn't really bother picking it up. it's a little fun, but i'd reckon there are better (and free?) alternatives from the same engine
